headline: Isoform-level and 3' end resolution is being built into single-cell, spatial and long-read resources
label: Isoform Resolved Transcriptome Tooling
summary: New tools and atlases resolve polyadenylation and transcript usage across single-cell, spatial and long-read data, extending to proteomic and aging contexts.
synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving transcript-level features, especially polyadenylation and isoform usage, and carrying them into downstream interpretation. scPolyA brings alternative polyadenylation analysis to single-cell and spatial 3' transcriptomes, while IsoAPA catalogs 2.3M transcript-resolved polyadenylation sites from long-read data across 816 sample groups. A mouse atlas of age-associated differential transcript usage in brain, liver and adipose finds mostly regulatory isoform switching and uses BioEMU to test structural effects. R2T2P links genome-guided assembly to translation profiling and proteomics to find novel RNAs. What is newer is the pairing of isoform resolution with interactive or agent-guided tooling, structural modeling and proteomic validation. Other items, such as perturbation screens, matrisome states and surfaceome profiling, are adjacent rather than isoform-focused.
